summary: A Georgia lookout list places a tennille tower in Washington County; no source found gives its build date, history or what remains today.

evidence.supports: Tennille entry: Washington County, coordinates, and 457 in the elevation column
The list says its towers come from the USGS name database
evidence.quote: Map shows GA fire towers listed by USGS name database (1-72) and as discovered

evidence.supports: Towers discovered on 1:100,000 USGS topographic maps
evidence.quote: on 1:100,000 USGS topo maps and NGS

evidence.supports: The list says it was motivated by a gap: no Georgia towers were listed at the FFLA site in 2010
evidence.quote: no Georgia towers were listed at the FFLA site in 2010

evidence.supports: GFC provided coordinates for 118 towers under the BLL numbering
evidence.quote: GFC provided coordinates for 118 towers (BLL-nnn) and

evidence.supports: An older GFC list described 203 towers under the gfc numbering
evidence.quote: an older GFC list described the locations of 203 towers (gfc-nnn).

evidence.supports: Column headings give elevation with no unit, and name the GFC number
evidence.quote: GA tower list lat/lon, elevation, GFC number

evidence.supports: Statewide shift from staffed tower operators to air patrol in the late 1980s
evidence.quote: In the late 1980s, the Georgia Forestry Commission began phasing out the tower operators in favor of an air patrol system.

notes_for_editor: Both sources are general: one county-level list entry, and a Vanishing Georgia post about a Clay County tower that gives statewide context only. No NHLR, FFLOS, Commons or other page for this tower was found. The list's elevation column (457) has no unit; the record's 139.3 m assumes feet. The Wikipedia town centre is 32.93806, -82.81056, so the list point lies a few kilometres west of town by my own calculation; no source confirms the exact site.
